# Navbar

The bar across the top of an app: your brand, the main links and a few controls, with the current page marked `aria-current="page"`. Below 640px the links collapse behind a menu button into a `Sheet` that slides in from the side; the brand and `actions` stay in the bar. Links render through `OuroProvider`'s `linkComponent`, so your router navigates.

```tsx
import { Navbar } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/navbar/navbar";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Navbar
  label="Main"
  brand={<Link href="/">Spoonjoy</Link>}
  items={[
    { label: "Recipes", href: "/recipes" },
    { label: "Cookbooks", href: "/cookbooks" },
  ]}
  currentPath={pathname}
  actions={<Button href="/recipes/new">New recipe</Button>}
/>
```

## Usage

Use `NavigationMenu` when a link opens a panel of further links, and `Tabs` for views of one page. `StackedLayout` puts a Navbar above the page.

## Use instead when

- Use `Sidebar` instead for more than a handful of destinations, or sections of them.

## Props

Type: `NavbarProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Controls at the end of the bar, at every width: a search button, an account `Menu`. |
| `brand` | `ReactNode` |  | Your logo or product name, at the start of the bar. Link it to the home page. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, position (`sticky top-0`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | The label of that sheet's close button. |
| `currentPath` | `string` |  | The path of the page being shown, from your router (`useLocation().pathname`, or `usePathname()` in Next.js). The link to that path, or else the longest link above it (`/recipes` for `/recipes/12`), gets `aria-current="page"` and the current look. |
| `items` (required) | `readonly NavbarItem[]` |  | The links, in order. Keep to the app's few main sections; a phone lists them in a sheet. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Names the navigation for screen readers ("Main"). It is not shown. |
| `menuLabel` | `string` | `"Menu"` | The name of the button that opens the links below 640px, and the title of the sheet it opens. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `children`: Not rendered. The bar is `items`, `brand` and `actions`.
- `links`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `items`: `<Navbar label="Main" items={[{ label: "Recipes", href: "/recipes" }]} />`.
- `logo`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `brand`: `<Navbar brand={<Logo />}>`.
- `pathname`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `currentPath`: `<Navbar currentPath={pathname}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `NavbarItem`

One link in a Navbar.

```ts
interface NavbarItem {
  /** The link's text: "Recipes". */
  label: string;
  /** Where it goes. Internal paths go through `OuroProvider`'s `linkComponent` (your router's link). */
  href: string;
  /**
   * Marks this link as the current page (`aria-current="page"`), when the Navbar's
   * `currentPath` cannot tell: a link whose page lives at another path.
   */
  current?: boolean | undefined;
}
```
